text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak says solution to peace process problems is connected to stopping Jewish settlements. He tells reporters after casting his vote in local elections that he hopes Clinton achieves good results in talks with Netanyahu in Washington.
- President says local elections pay important role in boosting economy and creating jobs. Elections run smoothly to choose 48,382 candidates.
- Clinton promises to do all he can to encourage resumption of peace talks.
- Ganzouri tells newpspaper editors that Mubarak will soon visit site of iron mine in Aswan.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Ebeid delivers verbal message from Mubarak to Qatari emir on ways to boost bilateral relations.
- Viktor Chernomyrdin says Russia regards Egypt as a strategic partner in the Middle East.
- World Bank and IMF to organise international conference in Paris on May 6-7 to boost development in Egypt.
- Foreign Minister Moussa tells Financial Times that Egypt seeks balanced formula for resumption of peace talks.
- Non-Aligned Movement condemns Israeli settlements on occupied territories and supports Arafat's call for special U.N. General Assembly session.
- Mubarak says freeze on Jewish settlements would solve all problems.
- 37 major companies submit offers for New Valley project.
- 1.7 million children born in Egypt every year, says Dr. Maher Mahran, head of National Population Council.
- Mubarak says cutting ties with Israel will not benefit stability.
- Public boycott of local elections -- National Democratic Party candidates and their thugs filled in the voting forms.
